definition: Nefarious means wicked and villainous in a calculated, scheming way — used for evil plots, schemes, and the people behind them.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word nefarious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know nefarious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In the spy film, the agent races to stop a nefarious plot to blackmail half the city's judges.
A shady deal merely cuts ethical corners, but a nefarious scheme is built on deliberate, calculated wrongdoing.
Diabolical goes even further than nefarious, suggesting evil so elaborate it seems almost demonic.

Villainous paints someone as the bad guy of a story — theatrical, mustache-twirling wickedness. Nefarious shares the villainy but points at the method: cold, calculated scheming, usually kept hidden. A villainous character may be loud and obvious; a nefarious one is quietly running the plot.

Iniquitous condemns something as grossly unjust and immoral — an iniquitous law, an iniquitous tax — with no hint of secrecy required. Nefarious adds the plotting: the wickedness is deliberate, schemed, and usually concealed. A rule can be iniquitous in plain sight; a nefarious scheme hides.

Sinister describes the feel of hidden menace — a sinister glance, a sinister quiet — hinting that evil may be at work without establishing it. Nefarious goes past hinting: the scheming wickedness is real and deliberate, not merely an atmosphere or a suspicion.
morally good and upright
principled and worthy of respect

Nefarious comes from Latin nefas, 'a wrong against divine law': ne- ('not') + fas ('what is divinely permitted'). Fas built no other English words, but it is related to fari, 'to speak' -- divine law was what the gods had spoken -- the root behind fate ('what has been spoken') and infant (literally 'one not yet able to speak'). So remember nefarious as behavior so wrong the gods would never speak it.
Nefarious means wicked and villainous in a calculated, scheming way — used for evil plots, schemes, and the people behind them.
Investigators finally untangled the accountant's nefarious scheme, which had quietly siphoned pension money into shell companies for a decade.
The scheme was deliberate, secretive, and sustained over years — exactly the calculated, plotting kind of wickedness nefarious describes, not a one-time lapse or an accident.

Use nefarious for a scheming person, plot, or scheme whose wickedness is deliberate and often secretive — 'a nefarious plot,' 'his nefarious dealings.' Keep it distinct from heinous, which describes one specific act so shockingly evil it provokes outrage: a nefarious mastermind may commit a heinous crime, but the mastermind and the plotting are what nefarious describes.

The ticket lottery looked scrupulously fair: a public drawing, numbered balls, a smiling auditor.
It took a bored graduate student three months of spreadsheets to see the nefarious design underneath.
Certain blocks of numbers never won — precisely the blocks sold in the poorest neighborhoods.

What made the fraud nefarious was not its size but its cold arithmetic: wickedness worked out in advance, then dressed up as chance.
